categories.main_business_segments: Mr Max Holdings operates primarily in the retail sector, focusing on discount stores that sell household electronics, daily necessities, apparel, and food products through self-service formats. The group also manages shopping centers and provides logistics (3PL) services to support its retail operations. All activities are reported as a single business segment centered on retail and related services.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company emphasizes efficient store operations through Everyday Low Price (EDLP) and Everyday Low Cost (EDLC) models, leveraging centralized procurement, private brand (PB) product development, and digital transformation (DX) initiatives such as self-checkout systems and an integrated online store. Logistics efficiency is enhanced by in-house 3PL operations and advanced inventory management systems.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Mr Max Holdings primarily serves general consumers seeking value and convenience, targeting families and individuals in suburban and regional areas. Its main markets are the discount retail sector, with a focus on daily necessities, food, electronics, and apparel, catering to cost-conscious shoppers.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates 57 stores mainly in Kyushu, Chugoku, and Kanto regions of Japan, with a dominant presence in northern Kyushu and the Tokyo metropolitan area. It also manages logistics centers in Fukuoka, Chiba, and Hiroshima, and has a small presence in China through a subsidiary in Shanghai.
categories.supply_chain_position: Mr Max Holdings is positioned at the downstream end of the supply chain as a retailer, directly interfacing with end consumers. It also manages midstream logistics through its 3PL subsidiary, supporting internal and some external logistics needs.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include expanding store count (especially in Kyushu and Kanto), strengthening omni-channel retail (targeting 10% of sales from online by 2029), pursuing M&A and new business opportunities, and enhancing operational efficiency through DX. The company is also focused on sustainability, supply chain optimization, and human capital development, though it does not engage in traditional R&D.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is primarily generated from direct product sales to consumers at discount stores, supplemented by online sales and rental income from shopping center tenants. Additional income comes from logistics services provided to group companies and external clients.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Key competitors include other discount retailers, supermarkets, home centers, and drugstores operating in the same regions, such as Don Quijote, Aeon, and local chains. Mr Max positions itself as a regional discount leader with a focus on low prices, broad product assortment, and operational efficiency.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending February 2025, consolidated revenue was 136.6 billion yen, with operating profit of 3.8 billion yen and net profit of 2.5 billion yen. The company has shown steady revenue growth (CAGR ~1.2% over five years), with a recent acceleration in profit growth due to improved gross margins and cost control. Total assets are approximately 83.2 billion yen, and the company employs around 689 regular staff (plus 1,678 part-time/temporary).
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Mr Max Holdings differentiates itself through its EDLP/EDLC strategy, offering a wide range of daily necessities at consistently low prices, supported by efficient logistics and private brand products. The company emphasizes convenience, value, and a customer-centric shopping experience, aiming to be an 'empowerment company' that enriches everyday life for its customers.
